It took 182 years. Most of the people who built it never saw it finished. ⛪ Watch Notre-Dame go up in 26 seconds. ⏱️

First stone in 1163. The choir came first, then the nave, held up by flying buttresses. Then the west façade, the great rose window and the twin 69 m towers. A 'forest' of oak beams under a lead roof. Largely complete by 1345: about seven generations of builders.

The twist: in 2019 fire took the roof and the spire. It was rebuilt with around 1,000 oaks and reopened in December 2024, in just five years.

Could you work on something you'd never see finished? Yes or no 👇

yt_description:
First stone 1163, choir first (altar consecrated 1182), the nave with flying buttresses, the west façade with its rose window and 69 m towers, the oak 'forest' roof, transept roses, largely complete by 1345. Viollet-le-Duc's spire came in the 1844–1869 restoration; fire on 15 April 2019 destroyed the spire and most of the roof; reopened 7–8 December 2024.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre-Dame_de_Paris
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
